model.method: Multiplicative seasonal decomposition + OLS linear trend

base.label: Base case
base.description: Current 2025-26 run-rate continues: Mainland-led volume growth with gradual yield drift.
drivers: Segment spending mix held at 2025 levels

upside.label: Strategy delivered
upside.description: Strategic pillars land: more overnight, long-haul and MICE visitors lift yield.

downside.label: Headwinds
downside.description: Weaker regional demand, strong HKD and Mainland outbound diversion to other destinations.

pillars.title: High-Value, Long-Haul Experience & MICE Diversification
pillars.tagline: From same-day shopping to overnight, experience-driven stays
rationale: Same-day visitors account for 54.3% of 2026 YTD arrivals but spend HK$1,139 per head vs HK$5,503 for overnight visitors (2025).
Long-haul markets are only 7.4% of arrivals despite the highest per-capita spend.
Yield per visitor moved from HK$3,333 (2024) to HK$3,167 (2025) as volume shifted to same-day trips.
Singapore earned HK$11,578 per visitor in 2025 vs HK$3,167 for Hong Kong.
initiatives: Scale 'CityWalk' neighbourhood trails (Sham Shui Po, Sai Kung, Central-Western) into bookable multi-day itineraries.
Long-haul air-capacity incentives and stopover packages with airline partners through HKIA.
MICE bid fund targeting association congresses at AsiaWorld-Expo, HKCEC and Kai Tak.
Night-time economy and cultural districts (WestK, M+, Palace Museum) bundled as premium overnight products.

timeline.action: Launch long-haul stopover campaign and MICE bid fund round.
Roll out 10 bookable CityWalk itineraries with OTA partners.
Review overnight conversion and per-capita spend uplift.

pillars.title: Mega-Events & "+ Tourism" Integration
pillars.tagline: Kai Tak Sports Park as a year-round demand engine
rationale: Tourism, convention & exhibition BRI stood at 59.8 (2015 = 100) in 2026-Q2, up 3.8% YoY - still well below its 2015 base.
Accommodation receipts in Q4 run 34% above Q3 on average - events can fill the softer quarter.
Seasonal index ranges 0.81-1.22: events can fill the softer June and September troughs.
initiatives: Anchor a 12-month mega-event calendar at Kai Tak Sports Park (concerts, rugby sevens, e-sports).
'Sports + Tourism', 'Culture + Tourism' bundles: event ticket + hotel + attraction passes.
Target shoulder months (Jun, Sep) with signature festivals to smooth seasonality.
Event-impact dashboard tracking incremental arrivals, hotel nights and spend per event.

timeline.action: Lock 2027 Kai Tak anchor events and ticket-bundle partners.
Run shoulder-season festivals; publish per-event impact reports.

pillars.title: Seamless Cross-Boundary GBA Multi-Destination Strategy
pillars.tagline: Hong Kong as the international gateway to the Greater Bay Area
rationale: 76.1% of 2026 YTD visitor entries came via land, HSR or HZMB control points.
Mainland visitors make up 78.3% of 2026 YTD arrivals; most are same-day.
International visitors increasingly combine Hong Kong with Shenzhen, Macao and Guangzhou in one trip.
initiatives: Joint 'One Trip, Multiple Destinations' packages with Macao and GBA cities.
Single-ticketing across HSR, HZMB and ferries with integrated attraction passes.
Optimise transit visa and 144-hour visa-free routing for international visitors via HKIA.
Convert same-day Mainland flows into overnight stays with evening events and hotel bundles.

timeline.action: Launch single-ticket pilot (HSR + HZMB + attraction pass).
Extend transit-visa routing campaign to long-haul source markets.

market_playbooks.headline: Turn the same-day majority into overnight stays and draw more visitors from beyond Guangdong.

initiatives: 'Stay the night' bundles sold at West Kowloon HSR and HZMB: evening event ticket + hotel + next-day attraction pass.
Weekday hotel and night-time offers (harbour cruise, night markets) for Greater Bay Area day-trippers on Xiaohongshu and Douyin.
Rewards for multi-entry permit holders who come back for a second and third overnight trip.
Market the Kai Tak concert and sports calendar in Shanghai, Beijing, Zhejiang and Jiangsu, where visitors arrive by air or HSR and stay longer.
Event-ticket presales bundled with HSR fares from non-Guangdong cities.

kpis.metric: Kai Tak Sports Park: rank among places visited

initiatives: Broaden the basket beyond shopping: dining, culture (WestK, Palace Museum) and wellness for repeat visitors.
Corporate MICE and incentive groups from tier-1 cities at HKCEC and AsiaWorld-Expo.

market_playbooks.headline: Loyal repeat visitors on short trips: give them new events and neighbourhoods to come back for.

initiatives: Cantopop concerts and cultural festivals sold as long-weekend packages with Taiwanese airlines.
Fresh CityWalk content for repeat visitors (Sham Shui Po, Tai O, Sai Kung) on Taiwanese travel media.
Hong Kong + Macao / Shenzhen combination itineraries for visitors who have 'done' Hong Kong.
Single ticket for ferry / HZMB transfers bundled with Hong Kong hotels.

market_playbooks.headline: A family-heavy, Disneyland-led market that slipped in 2026: family events and value bundles.

initiatives: School-holiday family festivals bundled with Hong Kong Disneyland and Ocean Park tickets.
Concerts by Filipino and international artists at Kai Tak with fan travel packages from Manila.
Hong Kong + Macao family itineraries with the ferry or HZMB transfer included.
Off-peak weekday hotel deals with Philippine low-cost carriers to fill shoulder months.

market_playbooks.headline: A growing long-haul market whose spend per visitor is falling: raise the value of each trip.

initiatives: Stopover packages with transpacific carriers through HKIA (free night, attraction pass).
Bid for association congresses and corporate MICE from US headquarters.
Sell Hong Kong as the gateway to Asia: Greater Bay Area and Macao add-ons priced into transpacific fares.
Promote 144-hour visa-free transit routing via HKIA to Mainland cities.

market_playbooks.headline: Short, first-time trips from Seoul and falling arrivals: use K-culture and events to restart growth.

initiatives: K-pop concerts and e-sports tournaments at Kai Tak with fan packages on Korean OTAs.
Night-time content (harbour, night markets, rooftop bars) for young first-timers on Korean social channels.
Café, dessert and photo-spot CityWalk trails designed to add a third night.
Weekend fare + hotel deals with Korean low-cost carriers.

market_playbooks.headline: The lowest spend per visitor of the 18 markets, among the shortest stays, and falling arrivals: give Japanese visitors reasons to stay longer.

initiatives: Gourmet and 'retro Hong Kong' itineraries (Cantonese dining, neon streets, film locations) with Japanese travel media and agents.
Three-night packages around Golden Week, Obon and Silver Week holidays.
Anime, J-pop and e-sports events at Kai Tak and AsiaWorld-Expo marketed to fans in Tokyo and Osaka.
Hong Kong Sevens and marathon packages for Japanese sports travellers.
Hong Kong + Macao / Shenzhen four-day itineraries for repeat visitors looking for something new.
Japanese-language guides and simplified ticketing for HZMB and ferry transfers.

market_playbooks.headline: Long stays and temple-led itineraries: build festival and faith-based culture products.

top_places: Che Kung Temple / Tin Hau Temple / Other Temples

initiatives: Temple and festival trails (Wong Tai Sin, Che Kung, Tin Hau, Cheung Chau Bun Festival) promoted in Bangkok.
Thai-language event packages around Songkran and year-end holidays.
Hong Kong + Macao / Guangzhou itineraries for second-time visitors.
Partner with Thai agents on multi-city fares that route through HKIA.

market_playbooks.headline: A fast-growing long-haul market with above-average spend: turn stopovers into stays and use sport as the hook.

initiatives: Stopover campaigns on Europe-bound routes via HKIA (two-night packages).
Hiking, beaches and outlying-island itineraries for active travellers.
Hong Kong Sevens and Kai Tak events packaged for Australian sports fans.
Clockenflap and food festivals marketed to young couples travelling together.

market_playbooks.headline: Older, loyal repeat visitors with few first-timers: premium experiences and new reasons to return.

initiatives: Premium dining, art (M+, Art Basel) and wellness weekends for repeat visitors.
Position Hong Kong for regional MICE from Singapore-based Asia headquarters.
Art Basel, Clockenflap and Sevens weekend packages.
Campaigns aimed at younger Singaporeans to bring in new first-time visitors.

market_playbooks.headline: High-spending, long-staying visitors from Mumbai, Delhi and Bangalore: MICE, incentives and celebrations.

initiatives: Incentive and MICE groups from corporates in Mumbai, Delhi and Bangalore.
Destination-wedding and celebration packages with hotels and venues.
Hong Kong + Macao + Shenzhen multi-city packages for first-time leisure visitors.
Vegetarian and Indian-dining guides bundled into itineraries.

market_playbooks.headline: A steady, flat-growth market: concerts, food festivals and heritage to lift demand.

initiatives: Concerts and food festivals packaged with Malaysian low-cost carriers.
Cantonese food-heritage trails promoted in Kuala Lumpur, Johor Bahru and Penang.
Hong Kong + Macao + Guangdong ancestral-hometown itineraries.
Rail and ferry passes bundled with Hong Kong hotel stays.

market_playbooks.headline: A fast-growing, long-staying market centred on Toronto and Vancouver, but spend per visitor fell in 2026.

initiatives: Heritage trips into Guangdong combined with Hong Kong stays for Toronto and Vancouver families.
Multi-city fares (Hong Kong + Greater Bay Area + Asia) with Canadian carriers.
'Homecoming' packages built around food, culture and family gatherings.
Off-peak promotions to spread long stays away from Christmas and Lunar New Year peaks.

market_playbooks.headline: Long stays and solid spend: stopovers, culture and nightlife.

initiatives: Stopover packages on routes to Australia and Southeast Asia.
Culture and nightlife itineraries (WestK, Old Town Central, Lan Kwai Fong).
Multi-destination Asia itineraries starting or ending in Hong Kong.
Promote 144-hour visa-free transit into the Greater Bay Area.

market_playbooks.headline: A family market that fell sharply in 2026: rebuild with family and Muslim-friendly products.

initiatives: Family theme-park bundles timed to Indonesian school holidays and Lebaran.
Muslim-friendly dining and prayer-room guide covering events and attractions.
Hong Kong + Macao packages through agents in Jakarta and Surabaya.
Ferry / HZMB transfers bundled at a single price.

market_playbooks.headline: A surging market made up mostly of first-timers: convert curiosity into longer stays and repeat visits.

initiatives: Winter-sun and city-break packages via direct and Gulf-hub flights.
Russian-language visitor information at major attractions and hotels.
New Year and winter festival packages.
Repeat-visit offers for first-time visitors (second-trip discounts with partner hotels).

market_playbooks.headline: A fast-growing, first-timer market with short stays and below-average spend.

initiatives: Link trade-fair travellers (Frankfurt, Munich) to HKCEC and AsiaWorld-Expo exhibitions.
Hiking and Geopark packages (Dragon's Back, Sai Kung) that add nights.
Hong Kong as the start of Greater Bay Area and Southeast Asia round trips.
German-language multi-destination itineraries with tour operators.

market_playbooks.headline: Culture-led first-timers with growing arrivals: art, design and gastronomy.

initiatives: Art and design itineraries (M+, Palace Museum, PMQ, Tai Kwun) with French media partners.
Gastronomy weeks pairing Hong Kong and French chefs.
Hong Kong + Macao + Guangzhou cultural-heritage circuits.
Multi-destination Asia itineraries through French tour operators.

market_playbooks.headline: The highest spend per visitor of all markets: luxury, Muslim-friendly and MICE.

initiatives: Luxury retail, family and Muslim-friendly hotel packages promoted in Saudi Arabia and the UAE.
Expand halal-certified dining and prayer facilities at major attractions.
Hong Kong + Macao + Greater Bay Area itineraries sold with Gulf carriers.
Turkish- and Arabic-language trip planning content.
